passage: In the clinic in Accra, Kwame gripped the edge of the chair. His heart thumped as he saw the little needle on the tray. Last time, someone had said, "It won't hurt at all," and it had. His eyes filled up and he began to cry. Dr Rania knelt down. "I'll tell you the truth, Kwame. It will pinch for a second, and I am here with you." Kwame sobbed but held out his arm. Dr Rania counted out loud. It pinched, and it was over. She said, "You were brave to stay."

qa.q: Where was Kwame when he saw the needle?
qa.a: Kwame was at a clinic in Accra.

qa.q: What was Kwame feeling as he looked at the needle?
qa.a: Kwame was scared and remembered a time it hurt after someone said it wouldn't. His thumping heart and tears show his fear.

qa.q: Why was Dr Rania's way of talking to Kwame wise?
qa.a: Dr Rania told the truth, that it would pinch for a second, and stayed with him. Saying it won't hurt makes the next visit harder because he stops trusting.

qa.q: How might Kwame's trust in adults change after this visit?
qa.a: Kwame may trust Dr Rania more because what she said matched what happened. Next time he may still be scared but feel less alone.

grounding: A child cries at the sight of a needle and heart thumps, and a doctor tells the truth that it will pinch for a second and stays, unlike a lie that makes the next visit harder.

passage:
From Irawati's baby book, written by her papa, Tenzin.
Today was the vaccination at the clinic. In the queue Irawati said, "Last time Nani said it won't hurt, and it did." She held my shirt so hard her knuckles went white, and cried. Her heart was thumping under my hand. The nurse knelt down and said, "It will pinch for a second, and I am here. Papa is here too." Irawati squeezed my hand. It was over fast. She sniffed and said, "Only a little pinch. She told the truth." She chose a star sticker.

qa.q: How was Irawati feeling in the queue?
qa.a: She was frightened, holding Papa's shirt tight and crying, with her heart thumping, because last time she had been told it wouldn't hurt.

qa.q: Why did the nurse's words help more than Nani's did last time?
qa.a: The nurse told the truth that it would pinch for a second and stayed with her, so Irawati could trust her.

qa.q: How might Tenzin feel with Irawati's heart thumping under his hand?
qa.a: He probably feels tender and a little anxious for her, wanting to keep her calm and safe.

grounding: A young girl is scared of a vaccination needle, and a nurse honestly says it will pinch for a second while staying with her.

passage: At the health centre in the village, Gautam hid behind his mother's sari when he saw the needle. "No! No!" he cried. His heart was thumping like a drum. His mother, Nandini, knelt. "It will pinch, beta. Just for a second. I am right here." "Will it hurt?" "A little pinch. Then it's finished." The nurse didi held up a toy parrot for him to look at. Gautam held Nandini's hand, squeezed his eyes shut and felt a sharp pinch. "Oh," he said, surprised. "That was all?" He wiped his tears and asked to hold the parrot.

qa.q: What did the nurse didi hold up for Gautam?
qa.a: She held up a toy parrot for him to look at.

qa.q: How was Gautam feeling when he saw the needle?
qa.a: He felt very scared, hiding behind his mother's sari with his heart thumping like a drum.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Nandini to say it would pinch?
qa.a: Telling the truth kept his trust, so the next visit won't feel like a trick.

qa.q: How might Nandini feel when Gautam says "That was all?"
qa.a: She likely feels relieved and proud of him for being brave. 😊

grounding: A young boy is scared of the needle, and his mother tells him the truth that it will pinch for a second and stays with him.
